clue.text: To get mechanical part to work, bang hard

definitions.text: To get mechanical part to work, bang hard

parts.words: To get mechanical part to work, bang hard
parts.note: the age-old fix for a jammed bit of machinery: give it a good thump to get it going again

explanation.surface: Advice for a stuck machine part: hit it hard to make it go.
explanation.definitionFit: To strike something with a heavy blow is the plain sense of the word, the treatment a stubborn mechanism often gets.

clue.text: An affair Othello, for example, mentioned

indicators.note: mentioned means the phrase is spoken, so we want a word sounding like it

parts.note: Shakespeare's Othello is a Moor, so he is 'a Moor'

explanation.surface: Othello's love affair is brought up in conversation.
explanation.walkthrough: Othello, Shakespeare's Moor of Venice, is 'a Moor'; said aloud that gives the French-derived word for a love affair.
explanation.definitionFit: A love affair, especially an illicit or secret one, is called by this borrowing from French.

clue.text: It's unfortunately clear to me I missed the start

definitions.text: It's unfortunately clear to me I missed the start

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things have gone wrong, so the letters of the words before it are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone realises with regret that they arrived after things began.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the anagram of CLEAR TO ME, signalled by 'unfortunately', and what a person arriving late would say.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who arrives after a performance or meeting has begun is exactly the person who has to admit missing its opening.

clue.text: Greek poet scholarship in Dark Ages largely ignored

indicators.note: most of the letters of the words scholarship in Dark Ages are disregarded, leaving a run tucked inside them

explanation.surface: An ancient Greek poet's learning went mostly unnoticed through the Dark Ages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'largely ignored' tells you to ignore most of 'scholarship in Dark Ages': the poet sits in scholarshiP IN DARk.
explanation.definitionFit: He was the celebrated lyric poet of ancient Thebes, famous for his odes to athletic victors.

clue.text: Aren't the insecure put at risk?

indicators.note: insecure means unsteady, so the letters of the words before it are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: A question asking whether people lacking confidence are in danger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'insecure' is the anagram signal applied to the letters of AREN'T THE (the apostrophe is ignored).
explanation.definitionFit: To menace or endanger something is to expose it to harm.

clue.text: Sporting event, unusually well supported

parts.note: a sports-day race where pairs run with two legs tied together, so each pair stands on an odd number of legs

explanation.surface: A sports occasion attracting an unexpectedly large crowd of fans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'well supported' looks like a big crowd; it means standing on more legs than usual, as a tied-together pair of runners do.
explanation.definitionFit: The school sports-day novelty race has partners bound at the ankle, giving the pair an odd number of limbs between them.

clue.text: Newtonian mechanics use it to measure refreshment service

definitions.text: Newtonian mechanics use it to measure

parts.note: rest refreshes, so a break is a refreshment
a Mass is a church service

explanation.surface: A physics textbook line about how classical mechanics weighs things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'refreshment service' looks like catering; it splits into a break and a church service.
explanation.definitionFit: The mass of a body when stationary is the quantity classical physics works with, since speed does not alter it there.

clue.text: A river flowed from this island

parts.note: flowed means ran, as water runs

explanation.surface: A river once flowed out of a certain island.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a Scottish island in the Firth of Clyde.

clue.text: Café produces last of the coffee, having let it stand around a short while

indicators.note: last of points to the final letter of the words that follow
around means the first piece wraps round the next ones

parts.note: stet is the proofreader's instruction meaning let it stand
min is short for minute, a short while

explanation.surface: A café serves the dregs of a coffee that was left standing a while.
explanation.walkthrough: STET is Latin 'let it stand', used by proofreaders. 'around' puts A MIN inside STET, after E from 'last of the coffee'.
explanation.definitionFit: This French word names a small bar or café, borrowed into English after soldiers met them in the First World War.

clue.text: Norwegian soldier coming from strong point in underclothes

parts.note: a fort is a strong point, a fortified position
bras are underclothes

explanation.surface: A Scandinavian soldier emerges from a fortress wearing his underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: The Norwegian soldier is the prince of Norway in Shakespeare's Hamlet.
explanation.definitionFit: The Norwegian prince in Hamlet leads an army and takes the Danish throne at the play's end.

clue.text: It is proper to speak of this mystery

indicators.note: to speak of means the word for proper is said aloud

parts.note: proper means right, as in the right way

explanation.surface: It is fitting to talk about this enigma.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mystery' is meant in the old religious sense of a sacred ceremony, not a puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: A mystery in the religious sense is a sacred ceremony, so the term for a formal ritual act fits.

clue.text: Fragments of cake grew untidy

indicators.note: untidy means messed up, so the letters of cake grew are jumbled

explanation.surface: A cake has grown messy and is in bits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'untidy' signals an anagram of CAKE GREW.
explanation.definitionFit: The broken remains of something destroyed are its scattered pieces.

clue.text: Lowest possible qualifications for cut-down degree course?

definitions.text: Lowest possible qualifications for cut-down degree course?

parts.words: Lowest possible qualifications for cut-down degree course?
parts.note: read as two parts, a small master of arts degree, the kind a shortened course would award; really the smallest values

explanation.surface: The bare entry requirements for a shortened university course.
explanation.walkthrough: Split it as MINI MA: a miniature Master of Arts, as a cut-down course might award.
explanation.definitionFit: The plural of the mathematical term for the least value a quantity reaches, the lowest points attained.

clue.text: Bede's mother set a precedent

parts.note: the first man, who set the example for all, and the forename coming before Bede in George Eliot's novel title

explanation.surface: The Venerable Bede's mother was a trailblazer.
explanation.walkthrough: Bede suggests the monk-historian, but the answer is the title hero of George Eliot's novel, who shares his name with the Bible's first man.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bible's first man came before everyone, and the same name heads Eliot's novel about the carpenter Bede.

clue.text: Clothe externally in good trousers, say

indicators.note: externally means the clothing word goes round the outside of the others

parts.note: to drape is to clothe in loose cloth
pi, short for pious, means good in crosswords

explanation.surface: Someone is told to dress on the outside in decent trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'externally' puts DRAPE round IN and PI (pious, so good). The answer names a style of very narrow trousers.
explanation.definitionFit: Very narrow tight-legged trousers, fashionable with 1950s Teddy boys, are named after the slim pipe for rainwater.

clue.text: It's right to pass to help me with no trumps

parts.note: to ease is to help or relieve
NT is the bridge abbreviation for no trumps

explanation.surface: Someone at the bridge table asks a partner to help by bidding no trumps.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads as a bridge call; it is a legal right to cross land. NT is the bridge abbreviation for no trumps.
explanation.definitionFit: In property law it is the legal entitlement to cross or use another's land, such as a right of way.

clue.text: Parade announced on All Fools' Day?

indicators.note: announced means the description of the date is spoken, so its sound gives the answer

parts.note: All Fools' Day is 1 April, by which time the third month of the year has gone by

explanation.surface: A procession is declared for the first of April.
explanation.walkthrough: On 1 April the previous month is over, 'March passed'; said aloud this sounds like the term for a ceremonial parade.
explanation.definitionFit: A ceremonial procession of troops filing past a saluting dignitary is a formal parade.

clue.text: Trio belt out the words.

indicators.note: out means put out of order, so the letters of trio belt are rearranged

explanation.surface: A singing trio belts out the lyrics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' signals the anagram of TRIO BELT.
explanation.definitionFit: The text of an opera or musical, as opposed to its music, is what the singers sing.

clue.text: Failing to make known the content of some farmers' job

indicators.note: the content of means one word becomes what is held inside the other

parts.note: failing means dying, giving out
to air an opinion is to make it known

explanation.surface: Not revealing what a farmer's work involves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the content of' makes AIR the filling of DYING. The definition is the work of farmers who keep milking herds.
explanation.definitionFit: Producing milk, butter and cheese from cows is the business of dairy farmers.

clue.text: Depression is hard for her

parts.note: a rut is a groove or depression in the ground
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Depression is a difficult experience for her.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Depression' looks like low mood; it is a groove worn in a track. The definition is just 'her', a woman's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Any woman's name can stand for a she, and this is the Moabite of the Old Testament book.

clue.text: Novel setting for pub games

parts.note: a bar is a pub
in tennis a set is a group of games

explanation.surface: Arranging a pub for darts and pool.
explanation.walkthrough: The novel setting is the county of Barsetshire in Anthony Trollope's novels, often shortened.
explanation.definitionFit: Trollope's imaginary English county, home of his cathedral-town novels, is a fictional backdrop.

clue.text: Amusement park won't open? How dishonest!

explanation.surface: A visitor is outraged that the funfair has stayed shut.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as UN-FAIR, a funfair that is undone or not open; as one word it means unjust.
explanation.definitionFit: An amusement park is a fair, so a closed one is whimsically un-; as an exclamation it complains of injustice.

clue.text: In the end, nearly the whole world was on top of him

definitions.text: the whole world was on top of him

indicators.note: nearly means not quite all, so the final letter of the phrase is dropped

parts.note: in the end means at last, finally

explanation.surface: Eventually he was carrying almost the entire planet on his shoulders.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth the Titan is condemned to hold up the heavens, often shown with the globe on his shoulders.
explanation.definitionFit: The Titan of Greek myth was made to bear the sky, usually pictured shouldering the globe.

clue.text: Poisonous growth on judge's head?

explanation.surface: A toxic lump appears on a judge's scalp.
explanation.walkthrough: British judges once put on a black cap before passing a sentence of execution.
explanation.definitionFit: A deadly toadstool shares its name with the black cap a judge donned to sentence someone to hang.

clue.text: A time to get up into cockpit

indicators.note: to get up in a down clue means to rise, so the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: an is the form of the article a before a vowel
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: Time for someone to climb into the pilot's seat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get up' turns AN ERA upside down in this down clue. A cockpit here is a pit for cockfights, so any place of combat.
explanation.definitionFit: A cockpit is an enclosure for cockfighting, hence any place of contest, like a stadium for combat.

clue.text: Scarlet desire

explanation.surface: A craving for bright red.
explanation.walkthrough: Scarlet is the surname of one of Robin Hood's merry men, whose first name is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Robin Hood's companion Scarlet bore this forename, and the word also means a wish or determination.

clue.text: Moved to see what one did unseen, perhaps

explanation.surface: Someone felt emotional watching what a person had done without being seen.
explanation.walkthrough: A bishop moved to another diocese (see) is said to be so; an 'unseen' is a passage given in an exam for rendering into another language.
explanation.definitionFit: Church usage for a bishop transferred to another diocese, and what a student did with an exam passage turned into English.

clue.text: They say a beech tree needs oxygen in dry surroundings

indicators.note: surroundings means the word for dry encloses the other pieces

parts.note: sere means dry and withered
the ash is a tree
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: Gardening advice that a beech tree needs air around it in drought.
explanation.walkthrough: 'They say' makes 'a beech' sound like a beach. The tree in the wordplay is ASH, which 'surroundings' places inside SERE with O.
explanation.definitionFit: A beach, the word that beech sounds like, is the strip of land beside the ocean.

clue.text: Brown, if it is held next to one, appears auburn

indicators.note: is held means the next pieces are kept inside the brown word

parts.note: tan is a light brown

indicators.note: next to means the two pieces sit side by side

explanation.surface: A brown shade looks reddish when set beside something else.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is the painter's name, used for the reddish-gold hair colour seen in his portraits.
explanation.definitionFit: The Venetian painter's name describes the bright reddish-brown hair he favoured.
